definition.def: If you describe an event, action, or procedure as symbolic, you mean that it represents an important change, although it has little practical effect.
examples: A lot of Latin-American officials are stressing the symbolic importance of the trip.
The move today was largely symbolic.

definition.def: Something that is symbolic of a person or thing is regarded or used as a symbol of them.
examples: Yellow clothes are worn as symbolic of spring. [+ of]

definition.def: Symbolic is used to describe things involving or relating to symbols.

examples.sentence: "The first Witte Fietsenplan was just a symbolic thing," he says.

Definitions range from discrete descriptions of various types of play such as physical, construction, language, or symbolic play (Miller & Almon 2009), to lists of broad criteria, based on observations and attitudes, that are meant to capture the essence of all play behaviors (e.g. Rubin et al. 1983).
And finally, for important public buildings, the architect may also be looking for a central symbolic idea on which to base the design.
The Australian Aborigines have recorded both real and symbolic images of their time on rock walls for many thousands of years.
